customer_signals.signal: A restaurant worker described paper schedules plus chaotic group texts causing missed shift swaps, side-work assignments and schedule confusion; another commenter praised read receipts, while others disliked over-messaging and app complexity.
customer_signals.limitation: Anecdotal thread; not representative demand evidence.

customer_signals.signal: Workers described communication apps being used for shift notes, prep, repairs and handovers, but also concerns about micromanagement and excessive messages.

early_findings: Café checklist and SOP templates are already a crowded low-price marketplace category. Competing on generic checklists alone is unlikely to be attractive.

A potential differentiation for the café kit is a highly curated, specialty-coffee-specific workflow pack with exceptionally low setup friction and genuinely useful manager routines; this remains unvalidated.
ShiftBrief AI faces established direct and adjacent software competitors. Dutch horeca products already bundle tasks, logbooks, messaging and scheduling at roughly €32–€49/month at entry levels.
Community signals suggest a real communication/handover problem, but also highlight a product risk: too many notifications, app complexity and perceived micromanagement.
No willingness-to-pay conclusion can be drawn from this scan.
next_validation: Interview or observe 5–8 independent specialty coffee shop owners/managers and 5–8 horeca shift leads; ask them to show current handover/checklist workflow before presenting a solution.
